Brawlhalla. El nombre solo ya debería ser suficiente advertencia. Una mezcla entre "brawl" y "Valhalla" que promete combates épicos dignos de guerreros nórdicos y entrega, en cambio, a tu rival haciendo el mismo sig con Lord Vraxx durante veinte minutos mientras tú te preguntas en qué momento exacto de tu vida tomaste la decisión que te llevó hasta aquí.
Empecemos por el principio, porque este juego tiene historia, y como toda historia trágica, merece ser contada desde su origen. Brawlhalla lleva desde 2017 disponible de manera oficial. Ocho años. En ese tiempo, la humanidad ha lanzado cohetes a Marte, desarrollado vacunas en tiempo récord, creado inteligencias artificiales capaces de mantener conversaciones filosóficas, y construido rascacielos completos desde los cimientos. El equipo de desarrollo de Brawlhalla, en ese mismo periodo histórico, no ha conseguido arreglar el netcode. No de forma significativa, no de forma que cualquier jugador que lleva más de un mes en el juego pueda notar. El netcode sigue siendo, con ligeras variaciones cosméticas, la misma experiencia de ruleta rusa digital que era cuando George RR Martin todavía generaba expectativas sobre Los Vientos del Invierno.

Hablemos del sistema de combate, que sobre el papel tiene una profundidad técnica real y ejecutada con cierta elegancia. Hay inputs, hay strings, hay combos, hay reads, hay edgeguarding, hay recoveries con lógica, hay un sistema de estadísticas entre armas que crea asimetrías interesantes. Todo esto existe. Todo esto está ahí, documentado, theorycrafteable, con potencial técnico suficiente como para que un jugador dedicado pueda pasarse años perfeccionando. El problema no es el juego en abstracto. El problema es la comunidad concreta que decidió ignorar absolutamente todo lo anterior y reducir el juego en su práctica real a una sola pregunta: ¿cuántos sigs seguidos puede hacer mi personaje antes de que el rival muera o me desconecte?
El sig, para quien no lo conozca, es el ataque de firma de cada leyenda, generalmente ejecutado con neutral especial o direccional especial, y que en la mayoría de los casos consiste en un movimiento amplio, rápido, con hitbox generosa y que en las manos de la comunidad media de Brawlhalla se convierte en el alfa y el omega de toda estrategia concebible. No hay edgeguard porque para hacer edgeguard hay que pensar en la posición del rival. No hay strings porque los strings requieren memorizar una secuencia. No hay reads porque leer al oponente implica que primero observas al oponente en lugar de mirar fijamente el botón que vas a pulsar. Lo que hay es sig. Sig. Sig. Sig. Y si no funcionó, más sig. Y si el rival esquivó, sig en otra dirección. Y si perdiste, fue porque el rival tiene el personaje roto y no porque lleves tres años jugando con una sola herramienta de un set completo.

El tema de los personajes rotos merece su propio apartado porque es quizás el fenómeno cultural más fascinante de Brawlhalla como ecosistema competitivo. En cualquier juego de peleas con un mínimo de historia competitiva, los tiers existen, hay personajes más poderosos que otros, y la comunidad debate razonadamente sobre balanceo. En Brawlhalla existe un meta completamente diferente: cualquier personaje que le haya ganado a alguien en las últimas veinticuatro horas está roto. Si te gana un Jaeyun, Jaeyun está roto. Si te gana una Cassidy, Cassidy está rota. Si te gana un Gnash con lanza y martillo, Gnash es un diseño inaceptable que Blue Mammoth debería retirar del juego inmediatamente y pedir perdón públicamente. El hecho de que esa misma leyenda haya sido derrotada contigo en las diez partidas anteriores es un dato estadísticamente irrelevante que la mente del jugador medio de Brawlhalla descarta con la misma eficiencia con la que descarta aprender a dodge en el momento correcto.
Este fenómeno se combina con otro igual de notable: la negación absoluta de responsabilidad personal como principio filosófico. En Brawlhalla no se pierde por jugar mal. Se pierde porque el rival es un spammer, porque el personaje está roto, porque el lag, porque el mapa tiene hitboxes extrañas, porque la luna estaba en cuarto menguante y afectó desfavorablemente a la caja de colisión del ataque. En los ocho años que lleva el juego, si sumas toda la responsabilidad que los jugadores de Brawlhalla han aceptado colectivamente por sus propias derrotas, obtienes una cantidad aproximada a cero. Es, en ese sentido, un logro de la psicología colectiva que merece estudio académico serio.

Pasemos ahora al modelo económico, que es donde Brawlhalla deja de ser simplemente un juego cuestionable y se convierte en un estudio de caso sobre ingeniería financiera aplicada al entretenimiento. El juego es free to play. Este hecho está técnicamente en lo correcto y espiritualmente en lo incorrecto, porque Brawlhalla ha construido alrededor de su gratuidad uno de los ecosistemas de monetización más elaborados que puede encontrarse en un título de su categoría.
El Mammoth Coin es, en primer lugar, una obra de arte de la psicología del consumo. No compras lo que quieres directamente. Compras Mammoth Coins en cantidades que vienen en packs predeterminados, y esos packs están diseñados con una precisión casi musical para que siempre te sobren o te falten monedas respecto a lo que quieres comprar. Quieres un skin que cuesta 140 coins. El pack más barato son 100. El siguiente son 200. Compras 200, te sobran 60. Ese skin nuevo que salió cuesta 100. Te faltan 40. Compras otros 100. Ahora tienes el skin y te sobran 60. Y el ciclo, eterno y perfecto como el movimiento de los planetas, continúa hasta el fin de los tiempos o de tu cuenta bancaria, lo que llegue antes.
Los crossovers con licencias externas merecen mención aparte porque son, en términos de precio por contenido, una hazaña. Pagar por una skin de un personaje de una propiedad intelectual que no tiene nada que ver con el juego, para aplicársela a una leyenda que jugarás con las mismas dos armas que siempre, haciendo los mismos dos movimientos que siempre, pero ahora con el skin de Finn de Hora de Aventura, es una transacción que solo tiene sentido emocional si la evalúas desde la perspectiva de alguien que lleva suficientes horas en el juego como para que su cerebro haya construido un vínculo afectivo con esos píxeles que supera cualquier evaluación racional de valor por dinero.

El sistema de ranked es donde la tragedia adquiere sus dimensiones más épicas. Brawlhalla tiene un sistema de escalada que va desde Tinplate hasta Valhallan, con múltiples divisiones intermedias, y que en teoría debería colocar a cada jugador frente a rivales de su mismo nivel de habilidad. En teoría. En la práctica, el matchmaking de Brawlhalla opera bajo una lógica que los físicos cuánticos describirían como "superposición de niveles", donde cualquier jugador puede aparecer en cualquier partida con cualquier otro jugador independientemente del rango, especialmente en las horas punta y en las horas valle y en las horas intermedias y básicamente en cualquier momento en que el servidor tenga más de doce personas conectadas.
El resultado es que Platino, que debería ser un rango medio-alto reservado a jugadores que han superado la curva básica de aprendizaje, se ha convertido en un vertedero de diversidad técnica tan amplia que en una sola sesión de ranked puedes enfrentarte a alguien que lleva doscientas horas sin haber aprendido que el dodge tiene invencibilidad, y tres partidas después cruzarte con alguien que ejecuta strings de siete hits con una consistencia que sugiere que lleva tres mil horas invertidas y que por algún motivo insondable del universo el sistema considera que tu nivel y el suyo son equivalentes. Esto no genera partidas competitivas. Genera partidas que oscilan entre el aburrimiento absoluto y la humillación clínica sin nada en el medio.

El peor juego de peleas que he jugado en mi vida. He jugado mas de 4000 horas en PlayStation y casi 100 en pc, y son las peores malditas horas desperdiciadas de mi vida. He gastado perfectamente mas de lo que una familia de clase obrera gana en 1 año solo en skins basuras y cofres que solo consiguen aumentar mi adiccion a las apuestas. El juego salio en 2017 (9 años) y la gente juega igual de mal que mi primo retrasado con down, y aun me atreveria a declarar que esa aberracion es mejor que los jugadores de esta porqueria. La gente no combea, no usa las mecanicas del juego y parece que tiene mierda de unicornio remplazando su materia gris. No se dedican a aprender las mecanicas del juego como leer al oponente, aprender a esquivar, mejorar su movimiento o estrategias, en su cabeza de nigeriano muerto de hambre es mas divertido solo spamear como retrasado el ataque pesado pensando que asi podra tener la atencion que nunca les dieron. Me he llegado a encontrar con anomalias que NO HAN USADO UN SOLO ATAQUE LIGERO EN TODA LA PARTIDA. En resumen el juego es una mierda sin sentido, lleno de subnormales que no aprenden las mecanicas simples de un juego de hace 9 años y que sus transacciones solo apoyan y fomentan la adiccion a las apuestas.

Newer players get thrown against people who treat the game like a full-time job, and the experience quickly devolves into watching the same repetitive garbage over and over again. Instead of rewarding skill, the game often feels like it's rewarding whoever is willing to abuse the most annoying tactics for the longest amount of time.

The developers deserve criticism for allowing so many frustrating aspects of the game to persist. Update after update, many of the same complaints continue to circulate throughout the community while players are left dealing with the same irritating mechanics and balance issues. It often feels as though genuine gameplay improvements take a back seat to everything else.

Brawlhalla isn't just bad—it's exhausting. It takes a genre that's supposed to be competitive and enjoyable and turns it into a constant stream of frustration, annoyance, and regret. There are countless games that respect your time and sanity more than this one ever will.

Brawlhalla Review

Since its release in 2017, Brawlhalla has pulled off a rare feat: establishing itself as the "people's Smash Bros" without ever feeling like a cheap, low-cost knockoff. It is a game that hides its depth incredibly well, and after all these years, here is my honest verdict, far from the usual clichés.
The Paradox of Simplicity: Easy to Pick Up, Brutal to Master

What strikes you first about Brawlhalla is how easy it is to read. Unlike Smash, where every character has a unique kit of 15 special attacks, Brawlhalla unifies its gameplay through a weapon system (Blasters, Scythe, Gauntlets, etc.).

    The Pro: If you know how to use the Scythe with Mirage, you (mostly) know how to use it with Mordex or Nix. This makes the game incredibly accessible at the start.

    The Con: Characters sharing the same weapon category can sometimes feel like "clones," with the only real differences being their three signature attacks (Sigs) and their base stats.

The true depth doesn’t come from the characters, but from the movement. The game's physics are surgically fluid. Dashes, gravity cancels (performing a grounded attack mid-air), and dodge management create an absolutely massive skill ceiling. To put it simply: it’s easy to have fun with friends, but in Ranked, the slightest positioning error results in a one-way ticket to the bottom of the screen.
The Business Model: The Gold Standard

You can't review Brawlhalla without praising its Free-to-Play model. It is one of the fairest in the gaming industry:

    Zero competitive advantages for purchase (absolutely no Pay-to-Win).

    Everything that impacts gameplay can be easily unlocked just by playing.

    Cosmetics (skins, massive crossovers with franchises like Steven Universe, WWE, or Avatar) are purely visual.

Where the Game Friction Lies (The Downsides)

It’s not all sunshine and rainbows after years on the market:

    The Community and Toxicity: The game can be extremely frustrating. Between Sig-spamming at lower ranks and players abusing emotes (looking at you, salt emoji), you need to have thick skin.

    The "Lethal League" Effect / Repetitiveness: If you play solo for hours on end, the core gameplay loop (waiting for a weapon, chaining mechanical combos, knocking opponents out) can get a bit redundant. It’s a game that shines in intense sessions but can get tiresome in the long run if you aren't actively trying to climb the ladder.

In Summary: My Verdict

    8.5 / 10

    Brawlhalla might lack the spectacular presentation or the emotional attachment of a Super Smash Bros, but it beats it hands down in two major areas: its cross-platform accessibility (the cross-play is flawless) and its netcode (the rollback is rock-solid).

    Whether you're here to tryhard in Ranked and master pixel-perfect Scythe combos, or just to let off some steam in FFA (Free for All), this project has matured beautifully. It's a staple of the platform fighter genre that thoroughly deserves its lasting success.

Stumble Guys, developed by Scopely, is a free-to-play party royale that leans heavily on chaotic obstacle courses and physics-based gameplay. At first glance, it appears to be a lighthearted, accessible multiplayer experience, but over time its design reveals a number of structural and technical issues that undermine long-term enjoyment.

The core gameplay revolves around navigating short obstacle courses while competing against dozens of other players. While initially entertaining, the mechanics remain extremely shallow. Movement feels loose, physics interactions are often inconsistent, and success can depend more on randomness than player skill. Reports of clumsy controls and unreliable physics further contribute to a lack of precision, especially in later rounds where timing is critical.

A defining issue with Stumble Guys is its reliance on repetition. Although the game includes multiple maps, the overall structure rarely changes—run, jump, avoid obstacles, repeat. Over time, the limited variety leads to a predictable loop that struggles to maintain engagement. Even player reviews frequently point out that the experience becomes repetitive and lacks meaningful evolution.

Technical problems are another major drawback. Players commonly report lag, crashes, and glitches that can directly impact gameplay. In a game built around timing and reaction speed, these issues can make matches feel unfair or even unplayable at times.

The multiplayer aspect, while central to the game, is also inconsistent. Many players have noted the presence of bots in matches, which reduces the sense of real competition and makes victories feel less rewarding. From community discussions, frustration also extends to balance issues and features like abilities or monetization, with some players describing the game as drifting toward a pay-to-win structure.

Creatively, the game has often been criticized for lacking originality. It closely mirrors the structure of Fall Guys, offering a similar format without significantly expanding on it. Critics have described it as a derivative experience that follows an established formula rather than innovating within the genre.

Visually, the game is bright and readable, but relatively basic. While the style fits its casual tone, it does little to distinguish the experience or enhance immersion. Combined with minimal progression depth, the presentation reinforces the game’s short-session appeal rather than encouraging long-term investment.

Ultimately, Stumble Guys delivers quick, chaotic fun, but struggles with repetition, technical issues, and limited originality.

In the end, it stands as a shallow and inconsistent multiplayer experience—best suited for brief sessions rather than sustained play, especially for those looking for deeper mechanics or more polished competition.
4/10

사람들이 게임을 못하는건 아닌데 너무 감정적입니다.
원래 이런 마피아 게임이 오해를 받을 수 있고, 오해를 할 수도 있고, 지목을 당할 수도 있고, 억울하게 죽을 수도 있어요.
그런 걸 감안하지 않고 이 게임을 하면 사사건건 당연히 화가 날 수밖에 없지 않나요? 뭐, 이렇게 예측불허한 게임에서 본인은 무조건 오래 살아남고 꼭 이겨야 된다고 생각하시는건지. 저도 여자지만 게임 내의 여자분들 목소리에서부터 머리 텅텅 빈게 느껴지던데, 합리적인 추리에도 불구하고 본인이 지목당하기만 하면 바로 성격 나빠지고 예민해져서 상대방 인격 모독하시는 분들 꽤나 많네요. 특히 채팅방은 더더욱 심하고요. 결국 까보면 범인이던데 감정적으로 굴어서 아득바득 분위기 망쳐가며 표 안 받아내다가 이기면 매우 좋아하면서 마치 논리적으로 사람들을 잘 구슬려서 이긴 듯이 자축하는거 보면 정말 삽으로 대가리 후려치고 싶네요. 그냥 죽었으면 좋겠어요. 당신은 이 지구에 쓸모가 없는 것 같아요.
정말 좋은 여자분들도 많이 뵈었는데, 비율상 남자보다 여자들이 더 머저리 같네요, 이 게임에선.
저의 이런 평가를 보고 반발심 들 사람들 꽤나 많을텐데요, 당신도 그런 부류입니다.
여자분들 죽고 나서 짜증난다고 찡찡대는 사람들 너무 많이 봤습니다. 
목소리는 성인인데 정신 연령은 너무 어린 것 같아요.
그래도 여자분들은 감정적이긴 하지 싸이코는 한 명도 못 봤는데, 남자분들중에 가뭄에 콩 나듯 개싸이코가 한 두명 있네요. 아예 인간의 삶을 포기한 듯해 보여요. 아예 마이크를 입 안에 넣고 괴성을 지르는 남자분도 봤고요, 다른 플레이어의 어머니를 욕하면서 '누구 애미 XX'라고 노래 부르듯 욕하는 남자분도 봤어요. 패드립하시는 분은 목소리에서부터 나이가 좀 있으시던데 당신 주변 이웃들은 당신이 그런 짓을 한다는걸 알고 있기는 한가요?ㅋㅋ
사람들이 참 비겁한게 채팅방과 마이크방의 사람들 상태가 많이 다르네요.
얼마나 비겁한지 얼굴조차 보이지 않고 서로 목소리만 들리는 게임인데도 채팅방에서 서로 그렇게 욕하던 깡다구가 마이크방에서는 거의 다 사라져있어요ㅋㅋ
그리고 마이크방에서 누가 실수로 채팅으로 상대방 인격 깎아내리다가 갑자기 마이크 되는 방인거 인지하고 바로 사과하는 모습도 봤고요. 왜 그러고 사세요?
그리고 범인이 지목을 당하면 당연히 본인이라고 쿨하게 까는 경우는 잘 없고, 이건 너무 당연한 현상인데요, 범인이 회피하는 모습을 보고 신고자가 바로 돌변해서 인성 뒤틀려지면서 상대방 인격 깎아내리는 분들 너무 많습니다. 특히 채팅방이요. 당연히 범인은 본인이 그랬다고 말 안하겠죠. 이건 뭐 인간 심리에 대해서 생각을 안하고 게임을 하시는 건지, 우선 뒤틀린 시각으로 상대방 꼬나보는 사람들 정말 정말 정말 많습니다...
표준어를 쓰면서도 상대방 비꼬다가 서로 말싸움하는 경우도 종종 봤습니다. 제발 욕을 안한다고 해서 상대방이 당신의 의도를 파악 못할거라고 생각하지 마세요. 보통 사람들은 당신 수준처럼 병신이 아닙니다!

솔직히 이건 게임 리뷰라기보다는 상황이나 말의 의도를 파악 못하고 무조건 화를 내고 보는 개멍청한 인간들에게 바치는 글입니다.

원래 멍청한 인간들이 화가 많거든요.

Goose Goose Duck is a multiplayer social deduction game developed and published by Gaggle Studios, Inc. that takes the familiar formula of hidden identities and player deception and expands it into a much larger, more feature-rich experience. While the game shares the core concept of innocent players attempting to identify hidden enemies among them, it greatly broadens the scope through an impressive selection of roles, larger player counts, built-in voice communication, multiple game modes, and a strong emphasis on social interaction. The result is a party game that thrives on unpredictability, turning every session into a unique mix of teamwork, suspicion, strategy, and chaos.

The central premise is deceptively simple. Players enter a match as members of different factions, most commonly Geese and Ducks. Geese are tasked with completing objectives and uncovering the identities of the hostile Ducks hiding among them. The Ducks, meanwhile, must secretly sabotage progress and eliminate the Geese without exposing themselves. This familiar setup immediately creates tension because every conversation, accusation, and explanation has the potential to influence the outcome of the match.

What truly separates Goose Goose Duck from many other games in the genre is the incredible variety of specialized roles. Rather than limiting players to basic categories, the game introduces dozens of unique characters with individual abilities and objectives. Some roles gather information, others manipulate evidence, while certain characters possess powers capable of completely changing the direction of a match. Because role combinations vary from game to game, players must constantly adapt their strategies and learn how different abilities interact with one another.

This role diversity dramatically increases replay value. Two matches rarely unfold in the same way because player abilities can alter investigations, create false leads, or reveal unexpected information. Even experienced players often find themselves surprised by situations they have never encountered before. The constantly changing dynamics ensure that the gameplay remains fresh despite the relatively straightforward foundation.

One of the game's strongest innovations is its proximity voice chat system. Instead of restricting communication to scheduled discussion phases, players can talk naturally while moving around the map. Conversations occur organically as players encounter one another, allowing alliances, arguments, suspicions, and deceptions to emerge in real time. This feature adds an entirely new layer of immersion because players can no longer rely solely on formal meetings to exchange information. Casual conversations become just as important as official discussions.

The social element is where Goose Goose Duck truly shines. Success depends far less on mechanical skill than on observation, communication, and psychological manipulation. Players must pay attention to behavior, detect inconsistencies in stories, and determine whether someone is genuinely helpful or secretly working against the group. A convincing lie can save a guilty player, while a poorly timed accusation can turn an innocent participant into a target. These interactions often create the most memorable moments in the game.

The maps themselves contribute significantly to the overall experience. Each environment features unique layouts, tasks, hidden pathways, and environmental interactions that influence how players gather information and move around the world. Learning the details of each map becomes an important skill because knowledge of the environment often provides valuable advantages during investigations and escapes.

The task system gives players meaningful objectives beyond simply discussing suspicions. Geese can contribute toward victory by completing assigned tasks scattered throughout the map. These activities provide structure to each match while also creating opportunities for Ducks to blend into the crowd or lure victims into isolated areas. The constant balance between completing objectives and remaining alert creates an enjoyable tension throughout every session.

Customization is another area where the game excels. Players can unlock a wide range of cosmetic items, outfits, accessories, and character appearances that allow them to personalize their geese and ducks. While these options do not affect gameplay balance, they add personality and encourage long-term engagement. The colorful visual style and humorous character designs help maintain a playful atmosphere even during particularly intense matches.

Visually, Goose Goose Duck embraces a bright and accessible cartoon aesthetic. Character models are expressive, environments are easy to navigate, and important gameplay information remains clearly visible. The presentation prioritizes readability and accessibility, ensuring that players can focus on communication and deduction rather than struggling with visual clutter.

The game's large player capacity is another significant advantage. Supporting more participants than many competing social deduction games allows for more complicated discussions, additional role combinations, and greater unpredictability. Larger groups create richer social dynamics because information becomes more difficult to verify and deception becomes easier to conceal. This added complexity enhances the overall experience for players who enjoy intricate social interactions.

The developers have also expanded the formula through additional game modes and special events. These alternative modes introduce different rules and objectives, providing welcome variety for players who want something beyond the standard deduction experience. Combined with frequent updates and new content, these additions help keep the community engaged over long periods.

The game is not entirely without flaws. New players may initially feel overwhelmed by the large number of roles and abilities. Understanding how every character functions requires time and experience. Additionally, the quality of matches often depends heavily on the willingness of participants to communicate and engage with the social aspects of the game. Poor communication can reduce the effectiveness of many mechanics. However, these issues become less significant once players familiarize themselves with the systems and find active groups.

What ultimately makes Goose Goose Duck stand out is its commitment to expanding every aspect of the social deduction genre. Rather than simply replicating an existing formula, it adds enough new mechanics, roles, and social features to create its own identity. Every match becomes a unique story shaped by player decisions, unexpected betrayals, clever deceptions, and dramatic last-minute revelations.

For fans of party games, hidden-role experiences, and multiplayer social interaction, Goose Goose Duck offers one of the most complete packages currently available. Its extensive role variety, strong communication tools, entertaining customization options, and consistently unpredictable gameplay make it a standout title within the genre. Whether playing with close friends or joining larger public lobbies, the game delivers a constant stream of memorable moments that keep players coming back for more.

Rating: 9/10
